proposal: The Mandate recommends housing higher education data at the Department of Labor to make postsecondary and workforce-training outcomes more transparent, place them in the context of broader trends, adjust real wages for regional differences in earnings and cost of living, and build a methodology for risk-adjusting institutional and program outcomes so they reflect value added rather than admissions selectivity (pp. 338 to 339).
remaining: Move higher education data collection and reporting to the Department of Labor (p. 338)
Adjust real wages for regional differences in earnings and cost of living (pp. 338 to 339)
Develop a risk-adjustment methodology for institutional and program outcomes (p. 339)

status_summary: No transfer of postsecondary data collection or the College Scorecard to the Department of Labor was found. The Department's 2025-11-18 announcement of a postsecondary partnership with Labor covers administration of most Higher Education Act grant programs and does not mention data functions. A different instrument, the final rule of 2026-07-01 (91 FR 40136) implementing the earnings provisions of Public Law 119-21, compares completers' median earnings with those of working adults with only a high school diploma, drawn from the institution's state or from national data; the Department's fact sheet does not describe a risk-adjustment or cost-of-living methodology.

timeline.event: The Department of Education announced a postsecondary education partnership with the Department of Labor in which Labor takes a greater role in administering most Higher Education Act postsecondary grant programs; the announcement does not describe a data transfer.

The Department published a final rule (91 FR 40136) implementing the Public Law 119-21 earnings provisions through an earnings premium test; it takes effect on 2027-07-01 except two instructions effective 2026-08-31.

title: House higher education data at Labor with regional wage and risk adjustment of outcomes
uncertainties: No transfer of postsecondary data or the College Scorecard to the Department of Labor was found, and no regional cost-of-living or risk adjustment of outcomes. The Labor and Education Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) carry no such entry. The 2026-07-01 earnings rule uses a state or national high school comparison group; its geographic section was read only in part, so a regional adjustment inside it cannot be excluded. S. 2511 would build a data system at NCES with no Labor role. The Labor newsroom listing was stale and enacted laws other than P.L. 119-21 were not read for data provisions. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
